Severe Flooding Disrupts Cable & Satellite Industry Operations Across Southern China

Operations across the Cable & Satellite industry in southern China have been significantly disrupted by ongoing severe flooding, which began after days of torrential rain swelled rivers and inundated low-lying areas in Guangxi and Guangdong provinces. The flooding, which local authorities describe as the most severe in over a decade, is currently affecting numerous uplink stations, ground facilities, and satellite signal relay sites owned by multiple companies in the region.

Among the impacted industry firms is Silver Stream Communications, which reports that floodwaters breached its Nanning broadcast uplink facility late Tuesday, forcing an immediate shutdown of all on-site equipment and evacuation of technical staff. “Our primary concern is the safety of our employees,” said Silver Stream’s operations manager, Chen Wen. “We have implemented all emergency procedures and are working closely with local responders.” The company has not provided a timeline for resuming full operations.

Elsewhere, Golden Sky Satellite confirmed that its signal processing hub in Foshan is under more than a meter of water, leading to the suspension of all local activities. “Staff have been relocated to higher ground and no injuries have occurred,” a spokesperson stated. The company is currently assessing damage to expensive ground station equipment and anticipates significant repair costs.

Workers at affected sites are being advised to stay away until floodwaters recede and structural inspections are completed. The National Cable & Satellite Industry Association estimates that over 1,200 workers across the region are currently unable to access their workplaces, with potential for extended disruption if heavy rain persists.

Industry analysts warn that the flooding’s impact on technical infrastructure could last for weeks. “The scale of the damage to ground stations is unprecedented in recent years,” said analyst Liu Jian at GlobalSat Research. “Companies face not only physical repairs but also complex restoration of sensitive signal equipment.”

The situation remains fluid, with ongoing rainfall complicating recovery efforts as firms coordinate with local authorities to safeguard facilities and personnel.
